The Aleksandrov-Kalashnikov AK-107 assault rifle was developed at the Izhevsk Machine-Building Plant based on the AK-74M. It is a representative of the AK "100-series". It features a balanced automatics system previously used in the AL-7 and AEK-971 models. This balanced system significantly improves burst fire accuracy from unstable firing positions, offering a 15–20% improvement compared to the AK-74M. However, this balanced recoil scheme was later abandoned for future AK derivatives. In 2011, the IZHMASH concern demonstrated an upgraded variant of the AK-107 as a potential replacement for the AK-74M. Lacking the original balanced mechanism, this variant features a redesigned receiver cover with an integrated Picatinny rail for quick and easy optics mounting. An adjustable aperture (diopter) sight was mounted at the rear of the receiver, replacing the traditional Kalashnikov open U-notch rear sight.
 
 %c[d_orange]ATTACHMENTS: 
 %c[d_blue] • %c[ui_gray_2] Suppressor: Rotor-43
 %c[d_blue] • %c[ui_gray_2] All scopes compatible with «Picatinny», «Weaver», and «Dovetail» mounts
 %c[d_blue] • %c[ui_gray_2] Underbarrel Grenade Launcher: GP-25 «Koster»
